speaker: Maya
text: Morning all. Quick AI platform sync: the support assistant, costs, and safety.

speaker: Chloe
text: Customers love the assistant, but some answers are simply made up.

speaker: Maya
text: Yes, that's hallucination: the LLM writes something fluent that isn't true.

speaker: Daniel
text: Part of it is the context window: we cut the conversation when it gets too long, so the model forgets the start.

speaker: Maya
text: Then let's ground it. We turn every help article into embeddings and pass the closest ones with each question.

speaker: Chloe
text: Does that make each answer more expensive?

speaker: Daniel
text: A bit. We pay per token, and the articles add about two thousand of them per question.

speaker: Daniel
text: Inference is now our biggest cloud cost, more than storage.

speaker: Maya
text: We could try distillation: train a small model to copy the big one on our own questions.

speaker: Daniel
text: A smaller model would also cut our GPU bill in half.

speaker: Chloe
text: And quality? I don't want to trade cost for wrong answers.

speaker: Maya
text: That's what evals are for: a fixed set of real questions we score after every change.

speaker: Maya
text: We have two hundred so far, graded by the support team.

speaker: Maya
text: {listener}, could you add twenty tricky billing questions to the test set this week?

speaker: Daniel
text: Thanks. Next topic is security.

speaker: Daniel
text: Someone tried prompt injection last week: they hid instructions in a ticket to make the bot reveal internal notes.

speaker: Chloe
text: Did it work?

speaker: Daniel
text: No, our guardrails caught it. They check every input and output against a list of rules.

speaker: Maya
text: We should also run a few red teaming sessions before the launch.

speaker: Chloe
text: Who does that? An outside firm?

speaker: Daniel
text: Internal first, with people from support and legal.

speaker: Maya
text: One more idea: an AI agent that can actually issue refunds, not just answer questions.

speaker: Chloe
text: That's exciting, but scary. What if it refunds the wrong customer?

speaker: Maya
text: We'd keep a human in the loop: the agent prepares the refund, a person approves it.

speaker: Daniel
text: And it would call our billing API with function calling, which the current model supports.

speaker: Chloe
text: Let's pilot it with ten percent of refund tickets.

speaker: Maya
text: Agreed. I'll write the pilot plan.

speaker: Daniel
text: I'll set up the small-model experiment and compare costs.

speaker: Chloe
text: {listener}, can you check with legal whether the agent may approve refunds under fifty euros on its own?

speaker: Maya
text: Great. Same time next week.
